idiom_name: typed IdempotencyStore port over an atomic claim (Map, SQL, Redis)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds no runtime primitive: the claim still comes from a Map/Set, an SQL upsert (Node's node:sqlite with ON CONFLICT, pg) or Redis SET NX, so the pattern becomes a typed port - `interface IdempotencyStore { claim(key: IdempotencyKey, ttlMs: number): Promise<boolean> }` - with one adapter per backing store and branded message-id types so a transport id cannot be passed where an idempotency key is expected. Behind a framework (NestJS interceptors, Effect, Temporal activities) the classic structure survives as middleware plus its store adapter.
pitfalls: Types are erased at runtime: branded ids catch key mix-ups at compile time but never make has() plus add() atomic.
Async claim APIs tempt hand-written adapters into await between check and insert; atomicity must live in the adapter's single primitive.
Adapters must agree on TTL semantics - a Map adapter that ignores ttlMs and a Redis adapter that honours it behave differently under test.
